167b.d: A reprint collection gathering six novels that follow Hiro Nakamura: Walls, Part 2; The Trial of the Black Bear; Past Experience; Baby Power; Stolen Fate; and The Trip, Part 1. Nothing in it was new -- it was a way back in for readers who had lost the thread.

1x00.d: The cut NBC never aired: longer than the broadcast premiere, differently assembled, and the only episode of the series that was never sold anywhere. It opens on Peter Petrelli standing at the edge of a New York rooftop, falling forward -- and waking in an apartment as Simone Deveaux comes in.

Making of the Damen Peak Video, Part 1.d: A two-part behind-the-scenes piece on the Damen Peak shorts, posted during the Heroes Reborn campaign and lost when the channel carrying it went down.

Making of the Damen Peak Video, Part 2.d: The second half of the Damen Peak making-of. Like the first, no copy is known to survive.

Season 1: 50 deleted scenes.d: Cut material from nineteen of the twenty-three episodes. Mostly extensions rather than lost plot -- the exception is Genesis, whose trims belong to the terrorist thread the series dropped. Runs about 49 min on the season one DVD.

Season 1: The Making of Heroes.d: The short official overview: where the idea came from, how the cast was found, the Comic-Con debut that made it a phenomenon before it aired. Runs about 10 min on the season one DVD.

Season 1: Special Effects.d: The difference between an effect done on set and one done in a computer, worked through on the scene where Hiro stops time in a Tokyo street. Runs about 9 min on the season one DVD.

Season 1: The Stunts.d: Stunt coordinator Ian Quinn on how the falls and fights were staged, with raw on-set footage of the takes. Runs about 10 min on the season one DVD.

Season 1: A Profile of Artist Tim Sale.d: The comics artist who painted everything Isaac Mendez paints, on his career and on working colour-blind. Runs about 11 min on the season one DVD.

Season 1: The Score.d: Wendy Melvoin and Lisa Coleman on writing and recording the series' music. Runs about 9 min on the season one DVD.

Season 1: Mind Reader game.d: A numerical parlour trick on disc five, dressed up as a test of Matt Parkman's telepathy. On the season one DVD.

Season 1 Episode Commentaries.d: 13 tracks on the season one DVD, covering the unaired pilot (Tim Kring alone), Godsend, The Fix, Distractions, Run!, Unexpected, Company Man, Parasite, .07%, Five Years Gone, The Hard Part, Landslide and How to Stop an Exploding Man. Cast, directors and writers rotate through each one rather than sitting the whole episode.

Season 2: Heroes Season Two: A New Begin.d: A promotional overview of the new season and its new characters, made to be watched before the episodes rather than after. Runs about 15 min on the season two set.

Season 2: Takezo Kensei: Sword Saint.d: A straight-faced fake documentary on the historical Kensei, complete with academics and period art, for a man who never existed. Runs about 24 min on the season two set.

Season 2: Global News Interactive / The.d: The in-fiction news report on Richard Drucker, collected from the campaign that ran online. Runs about 9 min on the season two set.

Season 2: Genetics of a Scene.d: Allan Arkush and Greg Beeman take a few scenes apart and explain what it took to shoot each one. Runs about 23 min on the season two set.

Season 2: Season Three Sneak Peek.d: Cast and crew promising the next year will be extraordinary, with almost no detail attached. Runs about 9 min on the season two set.

Season 2: 17 deleted scenes.d: Trims from six episodes -- an alternate opening for Nathan, more of Hiro in feudal Japan, more of Monica in New Orleans. Runs about 24 min on the season two set.

Season 2: Generations alternate ending.d: The finale as it was first cut, reusing much of the aired footage but sending the virus somewhere very different. Runs about 18 min on the season two set.

Season 2: Behind the Alternate Ending of.d: Tim Kring, Jeph Loeb and Jesse Alexander on why the ending changed -- the one place on any of these discs where the writers' strike is discussed directly. Runs about 11 min on the season two set.

Season 2: Untold Stories.d: Scenes shot for the twelfth and thirteenth episodes of a season that stopped at eleven. Mostly Elle hunting Sylar. Runs about 12 min on the season two set.

Season 2: NBC.com featurettes.d: Three web teasers made to look like camera-phone footage: Hotel Corinthian Explosion, Maya y Alejandro Viral Video, and Nathan and Peter Brooklyn Cam. Runs about 4 min on the season two set.

Season 2: Tim Sale Gallery of Screen Art.d: Close-ups of the paintings Sale made for the series. Runs about 2 min on the season two set.

Season 2 Episode Commentaries.d: 11 tracks on the season two set, covering all eleven episodes, from Four Months Later... to Powerless. Cast, directors and writers rotate through each one rather than sitting the whole episode.

Season 3: 36 minutes of deleted scenes.d: Includes the Hard Knox webisodes, cut in among the trims rather than listed as a series of their own. Runs about 36 min on the season three set.

Season 3: The Super Powers of Heroes.d: Stunt coordinator Tim Gilbert on staging the abilities, with before-effects footage of how the shots actually looked on set. Runs about 8 min on the season three set.

Season 3: Completing the Scene.d: The effects team on turning those plates into finished shots, including the ruined-future sequence. Runs about 8 min on the season three set.

Season 3: Alternate Stories: The Recruit.d: The five-part webisode series about the soldiers of Volume 3, collected on the discs. Runs about 18 min on the season three set.

Season 3: Alternate Stories: Going Posta.d: Echo's origin, the first Heroes webisode series, collected on the discs. Runs about 10 min on the season three set.

Season 3: Alternate Stories: Nowhere Man.d: Eric Doyle's story after his episodes, collected on the discs. Runs about 18 min on the season three set.

Season 3: Pinehearst Commercial.d: A mock advertisement for the company's civilian front. Runs about 1 min on the season three set.

Season 3: The Prop Box.d: A walk through the show's gold room, where the props worth keeping ended up -- including Isaac's original canvases. Runs about 5 min on the season three set.

Season 3: Genetics of a Scene.d: Four segments on specific shots: Claire's brain, the deformed test subject's prosthetics, Daphne's speed, and the Matt-and-Danko chase. Runs about 20 min on the season three set.

Season 3: The Writer's Forum.d: Tim Kring, Adam Armus and Aron Eli Coleite on what they were trying to do with the Villains and Fugitives volumes. Runs about 13 min on the season three set.

Season 3: Tim Sale Gallery of Screen Art.d: The season's paintings, including the ones painted onto rock. Runs about 1 min on the season three set.

Season 3 Episode Commentaries.d: 25 tracks on the season three set, covering all twenty-five episodes of Villains and Fugitives. Cast, directors and writers rotate through each one rather than sitting the whole episode.

Season 4: 45 minutes of deleted scenes.d: Trims across the season, spread over all four discs. Runs about 45 min on the season four set.

Season 4: Deconstructing Sylar.d: Zachary Quinto, Tim Kring and Adam Armus on the character the series could never quite finish with. Runs about 21 min on the season four set.

Season 4: Heroes Revolution.d: How the comics, the webisodes and the online campaign were meant to fit around the show. Runs about 11 min on the season four set.

Season 4: Milo Speaks.d: Milo Ventimiglia on comics, and on the ones he was publishing himself. Runs about 5 min on the season four set.

Season 4: Genetics of a Scene.d: The longest of these: several sequences taken apart shot by shot, including the car filling with water. Runs about 42 min on the season four set.

Season 4: Message from Tim Kring.d: Recorded after the cancellation and hidden before the last episode, saying the story was not finished. Runs about 4 min on the season four set.

Season 4: Sullivan Brothers Design Galle.d: Design work for the carnival. Runs about 2 min on the season four set.

Season 4: Heroes Connections.d: An on-disc chart of who is connected to whom, available from every disc in the set. On the season four set.

Season 4 Episode Commentaries.d: 4 tracks on the season four set, covering Once Upon a Time in Texas, Shadowboxing, The Fifth Stage and Brave New World. Cast, directors and writers rotate through each one rather than sitting the whole episode.

Heroes Reborn: 17 deleted scenes.d: Trims from nine of the thirteen episodes. Runs about 18 min on the Heroes Reborn set.

Heroes Reborn: Heroes Reborn: Reliving t.d: Tim Kring and the cast, old and new, on returning to the story five years after it ended. Runs about 11 min on the Heroes Reborn set.
